item.text:
**Bottom Line**
- **Yes, moderately stronger than inherited on balance, but not by a clean margin.** Jokowi left Indonesia with better macro stability, lower poverty, larger scale, and a more resilient policy framework than the inherited baseline, yet the trajectory was still held back by slower productivity growth, weaker middle-class/job outcomes, and incomplete structural reform under meaningful external headwinds.

**Claims**
- [Indonesia Economy Projected to Remain Resilient](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/24/indonesia-economy-projected-to-remain-resilient) — World Bank — 2024-06-24 — The Bank said Indonesia could still grow around 5.1% despite a subsiding commodity boom, food/energy volatility, and geopolitical uncertainty; it credited the government’s macro framework for attracting investment and keeping debt stable. IDs: `5B.10`, also `5B.6`, `5B.9`.
- [Indonesia: 2024 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Indonesia](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/08/07/indonesia-2024-article-iv-consultation-press-release-staff-report-and-statement-by-the-553165) — IMF — 2024-08-07 — IMF said growth remained strong despite external headwinds, inflation stayed in target, and the financial sector was resilient; that supports a “better trajectory than inherited” reading on macro management. IDs: `5B.10`, also `5B.9`, `5B.6`.
- [Indonesia Growth and Jobs Report Running Faster, for Longer: Structural Transformation, Productivity, and Good Jobs](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/indonesia/publication/indonesia-growth-and-jobs-report-running-faster-for-longer-structural-transformation-productivity-and-good-jobs) — World Bank — 2024 — The report says Indonesia became the world’s 16th-largest economy, unemployment fell from 9% to 5%, and poverty fell from 19% to 9% from 2000-2024; that is the strongest broad evidence that the economy ended the decade on a higher base than it started. IDs: `5B.10`, also `5B.6`, `5B.8`.
- [Macro Poverty Outlook for Indonesia: April 2024](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099847204042427165) — World Bank — 2024-04-03 — The Bank said growth was resilient and supported by domestic demand and services, and that prudent macro policies had built buffers through multiple shocks. IDs: `5B.10`, also `5B.9`, `5B.6`.
- [Macro Poverty Outlook for Indonesia: October 2024](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099026110152411280) — World Bank — 2024-10-02 — Poverty fell from 17.5% to 15.8% in 2024 while growth held around 5%, which supports the claim that Jokowi ended with a stronger broad welfare trajectory than he inherited. IDs: `5B.10`, also `5B.6`, `5B.8`.
- [Indonesia books lower-than-expected 2024 fiscal deficit](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/indonesias-budget-deficit-in-2024-at-23-of-gdp-3796361) — Reuters — 2025-01-05 — Reuters reported a 2024 deficit of 2.29% of GDP, below the legal 3% ceiling and below the earlier estimate; that supports competent fiscal stewardship into the transition. IDs: `5B.10`, also `5B.9`, `5B.6`.
- [Indonesia's dwindling middle class seen dimming economic outlook](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/indonesias-dwindling-middle-class-seen-dimming-economic-outlook-3610865) — Reuters — 2024-09-11 — Reuters described layoffs and fewer job opportunities pushing millions of working/middle-class Indonesians backward, which weakens the case that the gains were broadly durable. IDs: `5B.10`, also `5B.9`, `5B.8`.
- [Indonesia president orders audit of data centres after cyberattack](https://tech.yahoo.com/business/articles/bulk-indonesia-data-hit-cyberattack-075758741.html) — Reuters — 2024-06-28 — The cyberattack exposed that much affected data had not been backed up, showing real state-capacity fragility even as Jokowi responded with an audit; that is a negative on the “stronger trajectory” claim. IDs: `5B.10`, also `5B.9`, `5B.6`.
- [Analysis: A decade of Jokowi, Indonesia’s democracy icon, leaves illiberal legacy, critics say](https://theprint.in/world/analysis-a-decade-of-jokowi-indonesias-democracy-icon-leaves-illiberal-legacy-critics-say/2310394/) — Reuters via ThePrint — 2024-10-14 — Reuters’ end-of-term analysis emphasized strong growth and infrastructure but also patronage, dynastic politics, and weaker institutional integrity, implying some of the economic inheritance is politically fragile. IDs: `5B.10`, also `5B.5`, `5B.7`.
- [Indonesia hails Chinese firm as first foreign investor in troubled new capital](https://theprint.in/world/indonesia-hails-chinese-firm-as-first-foreign-investor-in-troubled-new-capital/2283073/) — Reuters via ThePrint — 2024-09-25 — The first foreign investment in Nusantara was real, but the project still had delays and weak foreign interest, so it does not fully prove a stronger broad-based trajectory. IDs: `5B.10`, also `5B.6`.

**Search Gap**
- No single source directly states the counterfactual “stronger than inherited” in those words; the conclusion is inferred from growth, inflation, poverty, debt, and jobs data.
- The clearest gap is **productivity and job quality**: evidence strongly supports macro stability and poverty reduction, but it is weaker on whether the economy is now on a decisively better long-run productivity path rather than just a stable one.
